findings.description: The script only validates that each settings file is a top-level JSON object before running jq over `.permissions.allow[]?` and `.permissions.deny[]?`. If either key exists with a non-array scalar value, jq exits nonzero under `set -e`, so the checker aborts instead of skipping the malformed settings file as documented.
findings.failure_mode: A user or project settings file like `{"permissions":{"allow":"Bash(git:*)"}}` causes `check-permissions.sh` to terminate with a jq error, producing an implementation-dependent non-2/non-1 failure rather than a WARN plus normal evaluation of the remaining layers. That violates the new documented behavior that malformed files are skipped and can break run preflight P2 unexpectedly.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the full expected shape before extracting rules, e.g. require `(.permissions.allow? // []) | type == "array"` and the same for deny, or make the extraction robust with `if (.permissions.allow? | type) == "array" then ... else empty end`; treat failures as WARN-and-skip for that file.
